title: Stamped bootstrap for satellite relay deployments: minimal-egress contract and upgrade acceptance
creator: Priya Sinha
description:
Overview:
This PRD defines a stamped-bootstrap flow for 'satellite relay' Private/VPC deployments where customer sites have tightly restricted egress (single-proxy or timeboxed mirror), intermittent connectivity, or operatorless environments. The goal is a deterministic, auditable bootstrap and upgrade contract that minimizes external network surfaces while preserving safe rollback and operator control for upgrades.

Why this exists:
Customers in regulated industries ask for a deterministic offline-friendly onboarding path for edge/satellite sites (small regional datacenters, air-gapped campuses, or partner-hosted nodes). Existing acceptance criteria focus on image mirroring and operator-mediated bootstrap; gaps remain for: (a) signed 'stamped' manifests that prove artifact provenance without live egress, (b) explicit relay/proxy handshake semantics for one-way mirror and ephemeral proxy windows, and (c) upgrade gates when control-plane connectivity is partial.

Success metrics:
- Automated bootstrap success rate >= 98% across supported mirror/relay topologies in staging tests.
- Zero post-upgrade critical incidents in canary cohort (first 10 sites).
- Time-to-bootstrap (manual steps) reduced by 60% versus current operator flow.
assumptions: Customer can provision a single outbound proxy (HTTP/HTTPS) or scheduled mirror window for artifacts
Customer provides reachable relay endpoint(s) for initial control handshake (TLS) or supplies signed mirror bundles
Operator has access to audited signed manifests (via Redwood signing service or customer KMS) for stamped bootstrapping
Air-gapped sites may accept physical media as a fallback; physical fallback is out of scope for automated acceptance tests but must be documented
non_goals: We will not design a fully offline package distribution system (complete physical media handling)
We will not change the operator UX for fully-managed Dedicated clusters outside of the bootstrap/handshake flow
We will not alter cryptographic primitives used for signing; we rely on existing artifact signing/KMS integration
requirements: Stamped manifest format: a compact signed JSON manifest that enumerates images, checksums, tokenized operator constraints, and minimum version pins
Handshake protocol: relay handshake must support one-time ephemeral tokens and mutual TLS verification between operator and satellite relay
Mirror window compatibility: bootstrap must succeed with scheduled mirror windows (configurable retry/backoff) and with single-proxy egress restricted to specific hosts/ports
Upgrade gating: runtime must refuse non-stamped upgrades when 'egress-locked' is configured unless explicit operator override is recorded in audit logs
Observability: telemetry emits a deterministic sequence of events for bootstrap and upgrade steps, with token- and manifest-level correlation IDs
Safety: automatic rollback criteria for upgrades when >10% of service routes fail health checks within 5m of cutover
Operator controls: console must expose a per-site 'allow-stamped-upgrade' action with required justification and audit trail
Compatibility: support for existing Private operatorless bootstrap modes (to avoid breaking current customers)
acceptance_criteria: Given a satellite relay with single-host egress proxy, staged bootstrap using a signed stamped manifest completes end-to-end in staging with no interactive operator steps
Given a scheduled mirror window, bootstrap completes automatically during the window and logs a deterministic manifest verification trace to telemetry
Upgrades attempted without stamped manifest are denied when site is configured as 'egress-locked' and an explicit console override is required
Audit logs record manifest signature verification, relay handshake outcome, and operator justification (if override used) with ISO-8601 timestamps
Canary cohort (10 sat sites) passes health checks post-upgrade for 72 hours with no rollback triggered
Integration tests covering failure modes (mirror partial, signature mismatch, proxy auth failure) return the correct failure code and remediation guidance
Security review completed and signed off by Security with documented threat model and mitigations
stakeholders: Engineering (Private Deploy): Diego Ramirez, Omar Haddad
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Design review and security threat model (2 weeks): finalize manifest spec and handshake API
Phase 1 - Implementation in Private operator (4 weeks): manifest verification, relay handshake, observability events
Phase 2 - Staging validation (2 weeks): run bootstrap matrix across mirror/proxy topologies and failure injection
Phase 3 - Canary (4 customers, up to 10 sites) with full telemetry retention and on-call support
Phase 4 - Gradual ramp: open to broader customers and document operator playbooks
telemetry: Emit events: stamped_manifest.received, stamped_manifest.verified, relay.handshake.start, relay.handshake.success, relay.handshake.fail, bootstrap.complete, upgrade.gated, upgrade.overridden
Include correlation_id, site_id, manifest_digest, signing_key_id, and operator_user in each event
Expose per-site bootstrap timelines in Console for debugging and audit
test_plan: Unit: manifest parsing and signature verification edge cases
Integration: full bootstrap flow against test relay with proxy, scheduled mirror, and offline mirror artifacts
Chaos: simulate partial mirror availability, TLS handshake timeout, and corrupted manifest
End-to-end: canary upgrades on 10 staging sites with automated health checks and rollback verification
notes:
Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Chose stamped manifests to allow offline verification without requiring continuous control-plane connectivity. This trades off operational flexibility (operator can no longer hot-push unsigned images) for stronger provenance guarantees.
- We will reuse Redwood signing service; customers requiring their own KMS will provide signing keys registered to the operator during onboarding.
- Mirror scheduling will be pluggable: operator can choose 'windowed mirror' or 'ephemeral proxy' mode per-site.

2026-03-12: Product/SE alignment meeting — agreed to support both Redwood-signed manifests and customer KMS-signed manifests; added audit requirements
2026-03-14: Updated acceptance criteria to require telemetry correlation IDs and 72-hour canary window after feedback from SRE
